results.content:
Flipcorder is a 1991 camcorder for your iPhone. You film little moments through the day, each one a “flip” (20 seconds by default), and they all land on that day’s dated tape. There’s no editing, so the chatter, the pauses and the fumble for the stop button stay in. Tonight, you play back one raw home movie in a warm VHS or crisp MiniDV look, date stamp and all.

I really wanted a way to capture those moments and keep authentic video alive - I feel we have lost so much chasing perfection for social media, that the messiness of a camcorder is appealing and comforting. Home movies can be for anyone, and Flipcorder is for those people. [...] I built it around iPhone Duo, which came out on Friday. The fold is the power switch: closed, the outer screen shows a lens cap; open it and the cap comes off. Fully open, the person you’re filming sees themselves on the outer screen with a red REC light. It works on every iPhone with iOS 26 or later too, with a big glowing POWER key instead.

A few things I cared about:  
• $4.99 once. No subscription, no ads, no watermarks, no account needed.  
• Your tapes stay on your phone unless you share them.  
• Never lose footage: closing the phone, a call or low storage always saves the flip.

Today launches v1.1.0 that includes earning stickers, subtle streaks for your home screen widgets, some in app events (like Halloween coming up) and more. I have a lot planned for Flipcorder! [...] Flipcorder

results.content:
The day tape

## Real tapes ran out. That was the charm.

A camcorder cassette held only so much, so you filmed the moments that mattered. Flipcorder keeps that limit, gently: short flips on purpose, one tape a day, and a fresh tape every midnight.

 0:20

  ### Flips, not footage.

  Twenty seconds is enough to catch the moment and get back to it. Want a longer take? Set Flip length to No limit in the camcorder’s settings. It’s the same app at the same price, with nothing to unlock.
 30:00

  ### A 30-minute tape every day.

  Like a real cassette, today’s tape holds 30 minutes, and the camcorder shows how much is left. When it’s full, a fresh one loads at midnight. A flip that runs into the end is cut short and saved, never lost.
 OFF

  ### Gentle reminders, if you want them. [...] ### Watch it like it’s 1991.

A tape playing: PLAY 0:00:01 over a sunset sea, with the cassette labelled Sun, Oct 4, 2 flips, 0:00:27 in the player below, and its eject, pause, look, delete, FLIP and TAPE, save and share keys.

Tonight, tap the day’s spine and the tape drops into the player. Its flips play back to back, like an old home video, tracking wobble and all.

### Save it your way.

The Save or Share menu: Camcorder look, just like the viewfinder, or Original (clean HD), the footage without any effects, with Cancel, Share and Save keys.

Save the whole tape to Photos as one movie that opens on a title card, in the camcorder look or as the clean HD original. Then share it straight from the camcorder.

The brief

## A 1991 camcorder in your pocket

Flipcorder is a retro camcorder for iPhone, made for iPhone Duo. You film little 20-second flips through your day, they land on that day's dated tape, and by tonight they play back as one home video. It's $4.99, paid once, and it's been out since October 23, 2026, the day iPhone Duo came out.

The Idea

## A fold that switches it on [...] In the iPhone Duo simulator

## A Camcorder You Open

The idea started from one line in the spec: open your iPhone Duo and it becomes a 1991 camcorder. A camcorder’s screen flips out to the side before you film, and the Duo opens the same way, so the fold could simply be the power switch, with the camera warming up as the phone opens and powering down, with your flip saved first, as it closes.

The app reads the hinge through UIKit, and it turns on at 30 degrees and off again only at 10 or below, so a phone held half open in a loose hand doesn’t flicker between the two. How fast the hinge moves feeds the picture too, and a quick snap open shows up as a little tracking glitch, as an old tape would. [...] The day tape

## Flips, Not Footage

What surprised me, as I built the app and used it myself on my iPhone 16, was the joy it brought me: the thunks and the sounds, and the filter itself, but also the joy of an unedited video of my day. So I explored leaning into that more, by limiting how long a flip can run and how long the cassette tape itself is.

The first version had no limits at all, so a recording ran until someone remembered to stop it, and a day’s tape could grow without end. On the third day of the build I changed the whole shape of it: every recording is now a flip that stops by itself at 20 seconds, with a calm countdown and no beeps, and every day gets one tape that holds 30 minutes, the way a VHS-C cassette did from 1989, around the time this camcorder is set.
